title: Workload Run Forensics (Multi-Run Scheduling and Crash Triage)
description: Read-only end-to-end forensics workflow for a GKE TPU JobSet series that won't schedule ('allows to fit only N out of M slice(s)') or keeps failing across runs. Recovers deleted JobSet specs from GKE audit logs, builds a per-run exclusion and placement table, decodes Kueue TAS buckets into 4x4x4 cubes, computes the per-run cube ledger and known-bad cube visibility, checks TPU_STDERR_LOG_LEVEL failure observability before searching for Megascale digests, and verifies every claim with ai-verify-failure-attribution.

step_notes.classify-workload-state: Step 0: Classify the workload or series of runs into NEVER_ADMITTED, ADMITTED_NOT_PLACED, PLACED_THEN_CRASHED, MIXED_UNSCHEDULED_AND_CRASHED, or HUNG from Kubernetes events and audit logs.
step_notes.list-jobset-runs: Step 1: Enumerate every run matching the workload prefix (including deleted or recreated runs that reuse a JobSet name) with created (PDT and UTC), admitted, and outcome timestamps.
step_notes.recover-jobset-spec-from-audit: Step 2: Recover each run's pod template from GKE audit io.k8s.batch.v1.jobs.create request bodies (jobset-controller-manager writes these even when jobsets.create is absent). Extract nodeSelector, NotIn node-pool exclusions, 4x4x4-state pin, and queue name per run; never infer one run's affinity from a sibling run.
step_notes.scheduled-events-by-pool: Step 3: Group Scheduled events by (run, node_pool) to see which started runs landed on suspect or known-bad pools (e.g. DCN-bad cubes).
step_notes.decode-tas-pending-message: Step 4: Read QuotaReserved / TAS messages in ascending order (--order=asc) to catch two-pass quota masking ('insufficient unused quota' hiding topology failure) and decode each 'excluded: affinity A, resource R, taint T' bucket into 4x4x4 cubes (divide by 16).
step_notes.cube-ledger: Steps 5 & 6: Compute the full cube ledger for each pending run (usable cubes allowed by state pin - self-excluded pools - cubes held by other queues = free cubes vs needed) without running a full pod LIST, and check whether known-bad pools are visible to the scheduler via cluster taints or only avoided by per-user NotIn lists. Any taint or cordon is a recommendation only (requires_approval: true; ask the user before running).
step_notes.check-failure-observability: Steps 8 & 10: Detect the framework (PyTorch/torch_xla, JAX, or Pathways) and effective TPU_STDERR_LOG_LEVEL / TPU_MIN_LOG_LEVEL from the pod spec. At the default TPU_STDERR_LOG_LEVEL=3 (FATAL), LOG(ERROR) Megascale digests ('Megascale detects a hang', 'Full error digest') never reach Cloud Logging; report the observability gap, recommend TPU_STDERR_LOG_LEVEL=2 and TPU_MIN_LOG_LEVEL=0, and skip broad digest searches. Also check whether any cited known bug's signature appears in this workload's logs; if 0 hits, label the link circumstantial.
step_notes.query-workload-logs: Step 9: Scope log queries to the coordinator pod (<jobset>-<job>-0-0 for PyTorch/MCJax, pathways-rm for Pathways) and narrow crash window to distinguish the hang digest branch from the non-hang 'Aborting the coordinator as an unrecoverable error is reported from one or more workers' branch ([[megascale-hang]]) and repeat-offender pools across runs ([[multi-workload-triage]]).
step_notes.resolve-workload-nodes: Before step 12, placed runs only (PLACED_THEN_CRASHED, MIXED_UNSCHEDULED_AND_CRASHED, HUNG): resolve each crashed run's node set over that run's window. Its result is the `node_set_json` that [[ai-verify-failure-attribution]] checks for COMPLETE scope.
step_notes.extract-culprit-hosts: Before step 12, placed runs only: quote culprit hosts from the crashed runs' own log lines. Its output file is the `culprit_hosts_file` that [[ai-verify-failure-attribution]] cross-checks every attribution against.
step_notes.ai-verify-failure-attribution: Step 12: Mandatory verification gate before publishing the report ([[run-forensics-report-template]]). Verifies run scope on every claim, time-aligned evidence, complete cube ledger accounting, 'would the remediation help?' math, and zero unapproved mutations. Pass the drafted report as `failure_table`. When no run was placed (NEVER_ADMITTED, ADMITTED_NOT_PLACED), skip [[resolve-workload-nodes]] and [[extract-culprit-hosts]] and pass 'not applicable: no run was placed' for `node_set_json` and `culprit_hosts_json`, so the gate checks the scheduling claims instead of inventing a node set.
